Non-Anemic.diet_recommendation: Maintain a balanced diet rich in iron sources to sustain healthy haemoglobin levels. Regular monitoring recommended.
food_list: Citrus fruits (orange, lemon) for vitamin C
foods_to_avoid: Excessive tea or coffee with meals (inhibits iron absorption)
High-calcium foods immediately before iron-rich meals
Non-Anemic.referral_action: No referral needed. Schedule routine check-up annually.

Mild.diet_recommendation: Increase daily intake of iron-rich foods. Pair iron sources with vitamin C to enhance absorption. Reduce consumption of iron inhibitors at meal times.
foods_to_avoid: Tea and coffee within 1 hour of meals
Calcium-rich dairy immediately before/after iron-rich meals
Foods high in phytates (unsoaked whole grains) without preparation
Mild.referral_action: Schedule appointment with primary care physician within 4 weeks for blood work confirmation.

Moderate.diet_recommendation: Implement a structured iron-rich dietary plan. Consume vitamin C with every iron-rich meal to maximise absorption. Medical consultation is strongly recommended to rule out underlying causes and evaluate iron supplementation.
food_list: Dark leafy greens (spinach, Swiss chard) daily
Liver or organ meat once per week
Orange juice or citrus with every iron-rich meal
supplements: Oral iron supplementation (ferrous sulphate 200mg) - as prescribed
Folic acid 400mcg daily if deficiency suspected
foods_to_avoid: Tea, coffee, and wine with meals
High-fibre bran immediately with iron-rich food
Moderate.referral_action: Medical consultation required within 2 weeks. Request CBC, serum ferritin, serum iron, and TIBC. Investigate underlying cause (nutritional deficiency vs. bleeding vs. chronic disease).

Severe.diet_recommendation: URGENT: Immediate medical evaluation is required. Dietary intervention alone is insufficient for severe anaemia. Nutritional changes should only be made under direct medical supervision alongside prescribed treatment.
food_list: Iron-rich foods as tolerated (not a substitute for medical treatment)
Liver and organ meats (high haem iron)
supplements: IV iron infusion may be required (hospital-administered)
Oral iron therapy under medical supervision
Blood transfusion may be necessary (medical decision)
Erythropoietin therapy if renal cause suspected
foods_to_avoid: Iron absorption inhibitors until HB levels stabilise
Severe.referral_action: IMMEDIATE referral to emergency care or haematology. Do not delay. Risk of cardiac complications at HB < 7 g/dL. Requires urgent full blood count, reticulocyte count, peripheral blood smear, and clinical assessment.
